The record now carries the four stable file paths with both selectors and the before/effective text, and my independent re-derivation from the SELECTED checker's own algorithm agrees exactly. machineProjectionCoverage.goodNews: X1 and X2 show coverage is better than the count of variants suggests: parentSelector and row order are both caught because the final check is a whole-list equality against a sort
machineProjectionCoverage.recordedGapNotRaisedAsAFinding: verify_projection.py loads parent and candidate BY PATH from --architecture and never compares them with the bytes/sha256 the record declares, so a record naming the right path with a wrong digest still passes (X4). The selected verify_design.py reads the same documents through pinned_bytes(...), so it IS pin-checked at selection. The frozen PASS therefore proves the projection is correct for whatever bytes are on disk, not for the pinned bytes the record names; a one-line digest check would make the helper self-contained. Not a required finding: the pins are verified independently in this review and by the selected checker at selection.
machineProjectionCoverage.forwardSelectionBinding: verify() asserts old['parent'] == record['parent'] for EVERY lock inheritance entry. All four share the v58 parent today. Consequences: the verifier is a pre-selection instrument by construction, since after selection the lock's entries carry the v59 pin as parent; and if the lock ever gains an inheritance entry for a different ancestor, the script fails on a change unrelated to this unit. The README states the first correctly; the second is worth knowing before the script is reused as a template.
